name: Duchy of Bar
alt: Barrois mouvant (the part west of the Meuse)

predecessors.name: Duchy of Lorraine
predecessors.text: 'Divided from Lorraine: 1033' (infobox); Sophia, who inherited on Frederick III's death in 1033, was 'the first person to associate the comital title with Bar'

successors.name: Duchy of Lorraine
successors.text: 'From 1480, it was united to the imperial Duchy of Lorraine'

ledger.x: 1033: the County of Bar emerges from Upper Lorraine.
1297: Philip IV invades Bar over Henry III's help to Edward I.
1301: the Treaty of Bruges ends Bar's war with Philip IV.
1354: the Count of Bar takes the ducal title and becomes a peer of France.
1430: Duke Louis dies and Bar passes to René I of Anjou.
1480: Bar is united with the Duchy of Lorraine under René II.
1480: the Duchy of Bar ends as a separate state in Lorraine (it passes to the French crown with Lorraine in 1766).

wars.name: Philip IV's invasion of Bar
wars.outcome: Philip IV invaded in 1297; by the Treaty of Bruges (1301) Henry III gave up some fortresses and held his county west of the Meuse as a fief of France (the Barrois mouvant); the east stayed imperial (the Barrois non-mouvant).

certainty.note: A frontier county with no boundary record on the pages.
The Meuse separates the French fief (Barrois mouvant) from the imperial east after the 1301 Treaty of Bruges; the line is the river, not a survey.
